Ui.Script:
-- ── GlobalStrings values this window uses (ref-GlobalStrings.lua, cited per line — the -- `X = X or "..."` idiom is this codebase's convention, CharacterFrame.xml/CastingBar.xml: -- a real GlobalStrings.lua, if one ever loads, wins over the fallback). Declared HERE and -- not borrowed from CharacterFrame.xml's identical line: load order must not be a hidden -- dependency between two windows (it bit exactly this file — the level line errored -- "string expected, got nil" when the window was driven without CharacterFrame loaded). PLAYER_LEVEL = PLAYER_LEVEL or "Level %d %s %s" -- :3075
-- The subframe roster (ref INSPECTFRAME_SUBFRAMES, l.2), now the reference's own two. Index -- N is tab N's page, and each page's `id=` is the same mapping written the other way round -- — the invariant CharacterFrame.xml states for its own row, and the reason `ToggleInspect` -- below can select the tab from the page rather than being told which one it is. BENILLA_INSPECTFRAME_SUBFRAMES = { "BenillaInspectPaperDollFrame", "BenillaInspectHonorFrame", }
-- The 19 inspect slots, in the ref's own `InspectPaperDollFrame_OnShow` order (l.60-78). -- Note there is NO ammo slot and NO bag buttons: a foreign player exposes neither. BENILLA_INSPECT_SLOTS = { "Head", "Neck", "Shoulder", "Back", "Chest", "Shirt", "Tabard", "Wrist", "Hands", "Waist", "Legs", "Feet", "Finger0", "Finger1", "Trinket0", "Trinket1", "MainHand", "SecondaryHand", "Ranged", }
-- ref InspectUnit: in the real client this is the FrameXML wrapper that load-on-demands the -- addon and then shows the frame. We have no LoD (header), so it IS the show path — kept -- under the real global name because that is what the UnitPopup row and any addon call. function InspectUnit(unit) BenillaInspectFrame_Show(unit) end
-- ref InspectFrame_Show (l.6-13) verbatim in shape: hide first, gate on CanInspect, request, -- remember the token, show. The CanInspect gate is the real client's `0x48a1b0` — a 10-yard -- d² test (wow-re §5-VERIFIED), which the app folds together with is-a-player and -- not-attackable (decision 0631 §"What the pin verified" 3/4). function BenillaInspectFrame_Show(unit) local frame = getglobal("BenillaInspectFrame") HideUIPanel(frame) if CanInspect(unit) then NotifyInspect(unit) frame.unit = unit ShowUIPanel(frame) end end
-- ref InspectFrame_OnLoad (l.15-25). UNIT_PORTRAIT_UPDATE is NOT registered in the ref -- either (its OnEvent has a branch for it, l.34-38, that can therefore never fire — a -- reference bug, transcribed as the ref behaves, not as it reads). function BenillaInspectFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("PARTY_MEMBERS_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_NAME_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MODEL_CHANGED") frame.unit = nil PanelTemplates_SetNumTabs(frame, 2) PanelTemplates_SetTab(frame, 1) end
-- ref InspectFrame_OnEvent (l.27-45). The retarget branch re-runs InspectUnit on the STORED -- TOKEN, so an inspect window follows a re-target — the token resolves to whoever is -- selected now. That is the ref's real behavior, not a quirk of ours. function BenillaInspectFrame_OnEvent(frame) if not frame:IsVisible() then return end if event == "PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED" or event == "PARTY_MEMBERS_CHANGED" then InspectUnit(frame.unit) elseif event == "UNIT_NAME_UPDATE" then if arg1 == frame.unit then getglobal("BenillaInspectNameText"):SetText(UnitName(arg1)) end end end
-- ref InspectFrame_OnShow (l.47-51), with ONE deliberate deviation: the unit is nil-guarded. -- The ref calls SetPortraitTexture(portrait, this.unit) unguarded, and `this.unit` is nil on -- any show that didn't come through InspectFrame_Show — `ToggleInspect` re-opening after -- OnHide cleared it is the reachable one. In the real client that leaks a swallowed Lua -- arg error every time (the same class decision 0413 caught in the merchant frame); ours -- would throw out of OnShow and abandon the rest of it, so the window would open with a -- stale name too. Guarding paints nothing instead, and the ref's own OnUpdate closes a -- target-less window on the next frame regardless. function BenillaInspectFrame_OnShow(frame) PlaySound("igCharacterInfoOpen") if frame.unit then SetPortraitTexture(getglobal("BenillaInspectFramePortrait"), frame.unit) getglobal("BenillaInspectNameText"):SetText(UnitName(frame.unit)) end end
-- ref InspectFrame_OnHide (l.53-59): drop the token, play the close sound, and tell the -- engine to stop inspecting (which stops the app's per-frame slot resolve). No subframe -- hide-loop is needed (unlike CharacterFrame_OnHide's): BOTH pages are true engine children -- of this frame — they are declared inside its own `<Frames>`, not as separate top-level -- files the way the character window's four are — so they hide on the parent's cascade. -- Dropping the token here is also what makes the honor page's nil check load-bearing: an -- `MSG_INSPECT_HONOR_STATS` reply can outlive the window that asked for it. function BenillaInspectFrame_OnHide(frame) frame.unit = nil PlaySound("igCharacterInfoClose") ClearInspectPlayer() end
-- ref ToggleInspect (l.67-83) + InspectFrame_ShowSubFrame (l.85-93). The ref's own "clicking -- the tab of the page already showing CLOSES the window" is kept rather than smoothed away, -- because that is what the real tab does. ToggleInspect is BARE (not Benilla-prefixed), the -- addon-facing name, matching this codebase's ToggleCharacter/ToggleQuestLog precedent. -- -- THE TAB ROW IS SELECTED HERE, from the page's own id, on every path — the line -- CharacterFrame.xml's `ToggleCharacter` carries and the defect it records (director, -- 2026-08-06: a page switch that did not move the row left the old tab enabled, and -- clicking it took the "already visible" arm and shut the window). This window could not -- show that defect while it had one tab; it can now, so the line lands with the second one -- rather than after the report. function ToggleInspect(tab) local subFrame = getglobal(tab) if not subFrame then return end local frame = getglobal("BenillaInspectFrame") PanelTemplates_SetTab(frame, subFrame:GetID()) if frame:IsVisible() then if subFrame:IsVisible() then HideUIPanel(frame) else PlaySound("igCharacterInfoTab") BenillaInspectFrame_ShowSubFrame(tab) end else ShowUIPanel(frame) BenillaInspectFrame_ShowSubFrame(tab) end end
function BenillaInspectFrame_ShowSubFrame(frameName) for _, name in ipairs(BENILLA_INSPECTFRAME_SUBFRAMES) do local subFrame = getglobal(name) if subFrame then if name == frameName then subFrame:Show() else subFrame:Hide() end end end end
-- ref InspectFrame_OnUpdate (l.61-65): the window closes the moment there is no target. -- The ref's behaviour kept, bluntness included — the ref checks "target" specifically, even -- when inspecting a party token, so inspecting a party member and then clearing your target -- closes the window. That is the shipped 1.12 behavior. function BenillaInspectFrame_OnUpdate(frame) if not UnitExists("target") then HideUIPanel(frame) end end
-- ── The paper-doll page (ref InspectPaperDollFrame.lua) ─────────────────────────────────
-- ref InspectPaperDollFrame_OnLoad (l.2-5). function BenillaInspectPaperDollFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MODEL_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_LEVEL") end
-- ref InspectPaperDollFrame_OnEvent (l.41-50). The model branch is a no-op for us: the pane -- samples the "inspect" booth slot, which the app re-bakes off the live unit's dressed look -- on its own (decision 0631 §4) — there is no `SetUnit` to re-issue. function BenillaInspectPaperDollFrame_OnEvent(frame) local unit = getglobal("BenillaInspectFrame").unit if arg1 and arg1 == unit and event == "UNIT_LEVEL" then BenillaInspectPaperDollFrame_SetLevel() end end
-- ref InspectPaperDollFrame_SetLevel (l.52-55). The "?" placeholders match -- CharacterFrame.xml's: UnitRace/UnitClass read nil for the one tick before the app's first -- snapshot for this token lands (an unguarded format() errors on nil), which for a foreign -- unit is a genuinely reachable window, not just a startup race. function BenillaInspectPaperDollFrame_SetLevel() local unit = getglobal("BenillaInspectFrame").unit getglobal("BenillaInspectLevelText"):SetText( format(PLAYER_LEVEL, UnitLevel(unit) or 0, UnitRace(unit) or "?", UnitClass(unit) or "?")) end
-- ref InspectPaperDollFrame_OnShow (l.57-79): the level line then all 19 slots. function BenillaInspectPaperDollFrame_OnShow() BenillaInspectPaperDollFrame_SetLevel() for _, slot in ipairs(BENILLA_INSPECT_SLOTS) do BenillaInspectSlot_Update(getglobal("BenillaInspect" .. slot .. "Slot")) end end
-- ref InspectPaperDollItemSlotButton_OnLoad (l.81-93). `strsub(slotName, 8)` in the ref -- strips its "Inspect" prefix to reach the GetInventorySlotInfo name; ours passes the bare -- name in, CharacterFrame.xml's own convention (the prefix is longer here anyway). function BenillaInspectSlot_OnLoad(button, slotName) button:RegisterEvent("UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED") local id, texture = GetInventorySlotInfo(slotName) button.invSlotId = id button.slotName = slotName button.emptyTexture = texture button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "IconTexture") -- No RegisterForDrag and no right-click: an inspected item cannot be picked up, used, or -- swapped. The ref registers no drag on these either — its OnClick (l.104-112) handles -- ONLY ctrl (dressing room) and shift (chat link), both named deferrals here, so this -- ships with the plain left-click registration and an inert handler. button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp") BenillaInspectSlot_Update(button) end
-- ref InspectPaperDollItemSlotButton_OnEvent (l.95-102): only the inspected unit's own -- inventory change repaints. function BenillaInspectSlot_OnEvent(button) if event == "UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED" and arg1 == getglobal("BenillaInspectFrame").unit then BenillaInspectSlot_Update(button) end end
-- ref InspectPaperDollItemSlotButton_OnClick (l.104-112): CTRL previews the inspected -- player's item on YOUR character in the dressing room (decision 1060), SHIFT posts its -- link to chat (decision 1059) — "link me that" being most of why anyone inspects. Both -- read through the unit-keyed `GetInventoryItemLink(unit, slot)`, the same binding the -- paper doll uses: a foreign player's worn items are PUBLIC descriptor data, so their -- links are as readable as our own (decision 0631's whole premise). Nothing else happens on -- a click here — the reference has no third branch, and an inspected item is not ours to -- pick up or use. function BenillaInspectSlot_OnClick(button, mouseButton) local unit = getglobal("BenillaInspectFrame").unit if IsControlKeyDown() then -- DressUpItemLink carries the reference's own nil guard (DressUpFrame.lua:11-13). DressUpItemLink(GetInventoryItemLink(unit, button.invSlotId)) elseif IsShiftKeyDown() then -- The visible-and-non-nil guards both live in the shared helper (UIParent.xml). -- Waiting on a template is the COMMON case at this window — an inspected player's -- gear is usually gear we have never seen — so the nil arm is a live path here, -- not a theoretical one. BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(GetInventoryItemLink(unit, button.invSlotId)) end end
-- ref InspectPaperDollItemSlotButton_Update (l.114-139). No count text and no broken tint: -- a foreign player's gear comes from the PUBLIC visible-item entries, which carry no stack -- count and no durability (decision 0631) — which is exactly why the reference's inspect -- window shows neither. SetItemButtonCount's 0 branch is therefore always the one taken, -- and is dropped with the count region. function BenillaInspectSlot_Update(button) local unit = getglobal("BenillaInspectFrame").unit local textureName = GetInventoryItemTexture(unit, button.invSlotId) if textureName then button.icon:SetTexture(textureName) else button.icon:SetTexture(button.emptyTexture) end -- ref l.130-138: a tooltip already owned by this button re-renders in place. if GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then BenillaInspectSlot_OnEnter(button) end end
-- ref InspectPaperDollItemSlotButtonTemplate's OnEnter (InspectPaperDollFrame.xml:18-28): -- SetInventoryItem against the INSPECTED unit, falling back to the slot-name string. function BenillaInspectSlot_OnEnter(button) GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") local unit = getglobal("BenillaInspectFrame").unit if not GameTooltip:SetInventoryItem(unit, button.invSlotId) then GameTooltip:SetText(getglobal(strupper(button.slotName)) or button.slotName) end GameTooltip:Show() end
-- ── The model pane (ref InspectModelFrame, l.24-39) ───────────────────────────────────── -- A booth-texture stand-in, not a live <PlayerModel> — the settled doctrine (0105's -- "I don't like 3d btw go for better 2d", 0208 §5, decision 0631 §4). `frame.facing` stands -- in for the ref's `model.rotation`; the ref's sign convention is preserved verbatim -- (rotate-left SUBTRACTS, rotate-right ADDS — ref l.29-39), as is its 0.61 default (l.25). function BenillaInspectModel_OnLoad(frame) frame.facing = 0.61 BenillaInspectModel_SetFacing(frame.facing) end
function BenillaInspectModel_RotateLeft(frame) frame.facing = frame.facing - 0.03 BenillaInspectModel_SetFacing(frame.facing) PlaySound("igInventoryRotateCharacter") end
function BenillaInspectModel_RotateRight(frame) frame.facing = frame.facing + 0.03 BenillaInspectModel_SetFacing(frame.facing) PlaySound("igInventoryRotateCharacter") end
-- The character window's twin (CharacterFrame.xml's BenillaPaperDollModel_OnUpdate — the -- same ref Model_OnUpdate, UIParent.lua:1444-1462, that EVERY 1.12 model pane wires: -- PaperDollFrame l.222-224, DressUpFrame.xml:202-204, TabardFrame.xml:406-408). Held button -- = half a turn per second; the 0.03 click above is the tap. The ref's held-vs-click sign -- flip is quoted, not corrected. function BenillaInspectModel_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) local step = elapsed * 2 * PI * ROTATIONS_PER_SECOND if getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "RotateLeftButton"):GetButtonState() == "PUSHED" then frame.facing = frame.facing + step if frame.facing < 0 then frame.facing = frame.facing + (2 * PI) end BenillaInspectModel_SetFacing(frame.facing) end if getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "RotateRightButton"):GetButtonState() == "PUSHED" then frame.facing = frame.facing - step if frame.facing > (2 * PI) then frame.facing = frame.facing - (2 * PI) end BenillaInspectModel_SetFacing(frame.facing) end end
-- ── The honor page (ref Blizzard_InspectUI/InspectHonorFrame.lua) ─────────────────────── -- -- WHY THIS PAGE WAITS WHERE THE PAPER DOLL DOES NOT. The gear page needs no round trip at -- all — worn items ride PUBLIC descriptor fields the server already streams (this file's -- header). A player's kill counters do not: they are private fields on their own object, -- which we never see, so they come over a request and a reply of their own -- (`MSG_INSPECT_HONOR_STATS`). Their RANK is the exception and rides the public bytes like -- the gear does, which is why the rank block can paint from the unit while the counters -- wait. function BenillaInspectHonorFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame:RegisterEvent("INSPECT_HONOR_UPDATE") end
function BenillaInspectHonorFrame_OnEvent() if event == "INSPECT_HONOR_UPDATE" then BenillaInspectHonorFrame_Update() end end
-- ref InspectHonorFrame_OnShow: ask only when this player's numbers are not already held, -- and repaint from them when they are. Both arms matter — the request arm is the first -- visit, the repaint arm is every visit after it, and skipping the request when the answer -- is already in hand is what keeps flipping between the two tabs from re-asking the server. function BenillaInspectHonorFrame_OnShow() if HasInspectHonorData() then BenillaInspectHonorFrame_Update() else RequestInspectHonorData() end end
function BenillaInspectHonorFrame_Update() -- THE TOKEN IS THIS WINDOW'S OWN, not the reference's hardcoded "target". The ref reads -- `UnitPVPRank("target")`/`UnitFactionGroup("target")` while its own paper doll reads -- `this.unit`, so inspecting a PARTY member paints that party member's gear under -- whoever you happen to be targeting's rank and faction colour. This window already -- tracks the token it was opened on (`BenillaInspectFrame_Show` stores it; every other -- read in this file goes through it), so the honor page reads it too and the two halves -- of one window agree about whose player they are showing. local unit = getglobal("BenillaInspectFrame").unit -- The token is nil'd when the window closes, and the reply is asynchronous: closing -- before it lands is an ordinary thing to do. The reference cannot notice, because -- "target" is still a unit; ours would paint a rank block for nobody, so it doesn't. if not unit then return end
-- Twelve figures in one call, in the order the reply's own body carries them. local sessionHK, sessionDK, yesterdayHK, yesterdayHonor, thisWeekHK, thisWeekHonor, lastWeekHK, lastWeekHonor, lastWeekStanding, lifetimeHK, lifetimeDK, lifetimeRank = GetInspectHonorData() -- The same twelve rows the character window's page paints, through the same painter -- (HonorFrame.xml) — one section per line, in the order they read down the page. BenillaHonorPane_SetRows("BenillaInspectHonorFrame", { CurrentHK = sessionHK, CurrentDK = sessionDK, YesterdayHK = yesterdayHK, YesterdayContribution = yesterdayHonor, ThisWeekHK = thisWeekHK, ThisWeekContribution = thisWeekHonor, LastWeekHK = lastWeekHK, LastWeekContribution = lastWeekHonor, LastWeekStanding = lastWeekStanding, LifeTimeHK = lifetimeHK, LifeTimeDK = lifetimeDK, LifeTimeRank = GetPVPRankInfo(lifetimeRank) or NONE, }) -- The rank block, off the unit for the rank and the reply for the bar. The two do come -- from different places and that is not an inconsistency: the rank is public unit state -- we can read at any time, the bar position is a private byte that only the reply -- carries. BenillaHonorPane_SetRank("BenillaInspectHonorFrame", UnitPVPRank(unit), GetInspectPVPRankProgress(), unit) end

Scripts.OnEnter: BenillaTooltip_AddNewbieTipFor(self, RANK, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.r, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.g, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.b, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_RANK)
BenillaTooltip_AddNewbieTipFor(self, RANK_POSITION, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.r, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.g, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.b, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_RANK_POSITION)
